Normalized Herfindahl–Hirschman Index

Source: R/hhi.R
get_nhhi.Rd

HHI rescaled so that it runs from 0 to 1 whatever the number of organizations, computed for each geography, subsector and year, with rollups for all subsectors (SUB = "ALL") and all geographies (GEO = "ALL").

Usage

get_nhhi(
  df,
  geography = "CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS",
  subsector = "NTEEV2",
  resource = "TOTREV",
  year = "TAXYEAR"
)

Arguments

df

A data frame with one row per organization-year.

geography

Name of the column that identifies the market's geography, such as "CENSUS_CBSA_FIPS" or "COUNTY_FIPS".

subsector

Name of the column that identifies the subsector. When it is "NTEEV2", the first three characters (the major group) are used.

resource

Name of the numeric column that measures organization size, such as "TOTREV", "TOTEXP" or "NETASS". Negative values are set to zero.

year

Name of the column that identifies the year, such as "TAXYEAR".

Value

A tibble with GEO, SUB, YEAR, N, the summed resource, HHI and NHHI.

Details

NHHI = (HHI - 1/N) / (1 - 1/N), where N is the number of organizations in the market. The formula is undefined for a single organization; such markets are monopolies and get NHHI = 1, consistent with HHI, CR1 and KWOKA. Markets whose resource total is zero get NA. Filter on N to exclude single-organization markets.

Examples

toy <- data.frame( GEO = c( "A", "A", "B" ), SUB = "ART", YEAR = 2020,
                   TOTREV = c( 75, 25, 10 ) )
get_nhhi( toy, geography = "GEO", subsector = "SUB", year = "YEAR" )
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   GEO   SUB    YEAR     N TOTREV   HHI  NHHI
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl> <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 A     ALL    2020     2    100 0.625 0.25 
#> 2 A     ART    2020     2    100 0.625 0.25 
#> 3 ALL   ALL    2020     3    110 0.525 0.287
#> 4 ALL   ART    2020     3    110 0.525 0.287
#> 5 B     ALL    2020     1     10 1     1    
#> 6 B     ART    2020     1     10 1     1
